bug_description.normalized: The staged reproducing checkout matches vulnerable commit `bd751a8bcd6d5d807665493e28993363884ec334`, and the saved ASan stack shows the crash in `prvTidygrowStack -> prvTidypush -> CleanSpaces`. The staged 16,384-byte witness (sha256 `404d4ef4d51c274ec8f30ebdce3f3d841b9c3632abb1855e2c6cb7c0ce24a85e`) is copied by `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` into `fuzz_inp`, NUL-terminated, and passed to `tidyParseString()`. `tidyDocParseString()` attaches that string to a `TidyBuffer`, `BufferInput()` wraps it as the active stream, and `DocParseStream()` dispatches the non-XML run into `ParseDocument()`. `ParseDocument()` tokenizes the HTML-like bytes and recursive insertion helpers link the resulting nodes into DOM `content`/`next` lists. `CleanSpaces()` then traverses that tree with an explicit stack initialized at capacity 16 and `top = -1`. Earlier non-null executions of `stack->firstNode[++stack->top] = node` on the witnessed path must raise `top` to 15 before the crashing call, because the saved sink later copies 16 pointers (`WRITE of size 128` on an 8-byte-pointer build). The next descent therefore reaches `push()` with a logically full stack, `growStack()` derives `new_capacity = 32`, allocates only 32 bytes instead of 32 `Node*` slots, and `memcpy()` copies 128 bytes into that undersized destination. The staged patch fixes the root cause by changing the allocation to `new_capacity * sizeof(Node**)` before the copy.

source.description: First project-side materialization of attacker-controlled input on the vulnerable path. `tidyDocParseString()` attaches the harness-provided string to `inbuf`, creating the `TidyBuffer` state that `BufferInput()` and the HTML parser later consume.
source.value_from: The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_36694/poc` is 16,384 bytes (sha256 `404d4ef4d51c274ec8f30ebdce3f3d841b9c3632abb1855e2c6cb7c0ce24a85e`). In the staged harness `tidy_parse_string_fuzzer.c:39-42`, those bytes are copied into `fuzz_inp`, terminated with `\0`, and passed to `tidyParseString()` at line 29. This call attaches that exact NUL-terminated buffer to `inbuf`.

sink.description: ASan-observed sink. `growStack()` copies `top + 1` saved node pointers into the replacement buffer, but step 12 allocated only 32 bytes. With `top == 15`, this line copies 128 bytes into that 32-byte heap region.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `growStack()` treats logical slot count `new_capacity` as a byte count and allocates only 32 bytes when doubling a 16-entry `Node*` stack. The staged fix multiplies by `sizeof(Node**)`, making the allocation large enough for 32 pointers before the copy.

parser_admitted.description: On the reproduced run `xmlIn` is false, so `DocParseStream()` dispatches to the HTML parser `ParseDocument()` on the attached witness stream.

cleanup_reached.description: `ParseDocument()` always invokes `CleanSpaces()` on the constructed root before returning, and the saved ASan crash stack includes `CleanSpaces` immediately below `push()` and `growStack()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This helper wires each parsed node into its parent's child and sibling lists. Repeated caller-side use on tokens from `ParseDocument()` is the concrete origin of the `content` and `next` relationships that `CleanSpaces()` later traverses and stores on its explicit stack.

coarse_trace.summary: The NUL-terminated witness is attached to `inbuf`, wrapped by `BufferInput()`, installed as `doc->docIn`, and dispatched by `DocParseStream()` into the non-XML `ParseDocument()` path.
`GetToken()` materializes attacker-controlled tokens from that stream, and recursive insertion helpers link them into DOM `content`/`next` relations.
`CleanSpaces()` walks the DOM with an explicit 16-slot stack of pending `next` pointers; earlier non-null `push()` stores raise `top` to 15, and the next descent triggers the full-stack branch.

The grow path doubles logical capacity to 32 but allocates only 32 bytes, then `memcpy()` copies 16 saved pointers (128 bytes) into that undersized buffer, matching the ASan heap-buffer-overflow WRITE.

fine_trace.note: Source. `tidyDocParseString()` attaches the attacker-controlled NUL-terminated string to `inbuf`; later parser reads come from this exact buffer.

`BufferInput()` wraps the attached `TidyBuffer` in a `StreamIn`. This call reaches `tidyInitInputBuffer()` in `src/buffio.c`, which stores `buf` as `in->source.sourceData`, so future `ReadByte()` operations consume the witness bytes from step 1.
`DocParseStream()` installs that `StreamIn` as the document's active input source, making the attached witness available to the lexer and parser through `doc->docIn`.
On the reproduced run `xmlIn` is false, so `DocParseStream()` takes the HTML-parser branch and hands the active input stream from step 3 to `ParseDocument()`.

`ParseDocument()` repeatedly materializes tokens from `doc->docIn`. In the staged witness these bytes include repeated tag-like fragments such as `<base`, `<dt`, `<ul`, `<A`, `<tr`, `<HR`, `<th`, and `<p`.

Recursive parser helpers use these assignments to wire each attacker-derived token into parent-child and sibling links. Repeated insertions create the DOM `content`/`next` structure later traversed by `CleanSpaces()`.
Before the cleanup walk, `CleanSpaces()` allocates an explicit node stack with logical capacity 16. `newStack()` initializes `top = -1` and allocates `firstNode` for 16 `Node*` entries.

Earlier in the same `CleanSpaces()` walk, every non-null pending sibling executes this store and increments `top`. Because step 7 started at `top = -1` and the saved sink later copies 16 entries (`WRITE of size 128` on an 8-byte-pointer build), the witnessed path must have driven this line 16 times before the crashing call, leaving `top == 15`.

At the crashing visit, `CleanSpaces()` reaches another node with children and calls `push(stack, next)` before following `node->content`. Because `push()` checks fullness before `if (node)`, reaching this branch with `top == 15` is enough to take the grow path even if the current `next` is NULL.
`push()` compares the current depth against the 16-slot capacity and calls `growStack()` when full. Here `stackFull(stack)` is true because `top == capacity - 1`, i.e. `15 == 16 - 1`.
The grow helper derives a new logical capacity of 32 pointer slots from the full 16-slot stack.

Root cause. The reallocation uses logical slot count `new_capacity` as a byte count and allocates only 32 bytes. The saved ASan allocation context names this line and reports the resulting destination region as 32 bytes `[0x6030000000a0, 0x6030000000c0)`.

Sink. The copy length is `sizeof(Node**) * (stack->top + 1)` = `8 * 16` = 128 bytes, so `memcpy()` overruns the 32-byte destination from step 12 by 96 bytes. This matches the saved ASan `WRITE of size 128` at line 4482.

format.name: NUL-terminated HTML-like witness
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged 16,384-byte file `poc` (sha256 `404d4ef4d51c274ec8f30ebdce3f3d841b9c3632abb1855e2c6cb7c0ce24a85e`). The harness must still copy it, append `\0`, and pass it to `tidyParseString()`. The resulting parse must still build a DOM whose `CleanSpaces()` walk performs sixteen earlier non-null `stack->firstNode[++stack->top] = node` stores so `top` is 15 when a later content-bearing node calls `push()` again and enters `growStack()`. The current evidence does not justify a broader input class than witnesses preserving that same parser-to-cleanup behavior.
